items: **Push-to-talk talk notifications.** When someone talks on a channel you belong to but have not joined, MonoPhone shows "is talking" with a Join button; Join plays the rest of the live transmission. Notifications are limited to one every two minutes per channel, follow Do not disturb and can be turned off for each channel.
**Every device hears push-to-talk.** All devices of the same extension now hear live push-to-talk audio and get its notifications; only the device that is talking is left out.

**Quick push-to-talk channels.** Switch channels from the push-to-talk pill on the Keypad, keep up to three favourite channels as chips, and start a private channel with one or more colleagues from People. Favourites come first in the iPhone widget channel picker and on Apple Watch.
**Online members in push-to-talk.** The channel page and the Keypad pill show who is online.

**Starter examples for new companies.** A new company can start with ready-made examples: four extensions, a sales ring group, a support queue, office hours with a holiday, a main menu and call flows, all marked "(example)". Choose it in the setup wizard or when you create a company; existing companies add them from System, Setup guide. Examples use no licence seats and never touch your trunks or numbers.

**AI and GIF steps in the setup wizard.** Optional steps set up an AI provider from a list of presets (with where to get a key and a key test) and GIF search with a GIPHY key. Admin, AI, Add provider offers the same presets, and Test key now works for every provider kind, including speech services.

**Stickers in team chat.** A sticker button in the MonoPhone message field opens a panel with GIFs and Stickers tabs: favourites, recently sent stickers, your own stickers made from photos, and GIPHY stickers when GIF search is on. Favourites and your own stickers follow you on every device. Stickers show without a bubble, and the web chat now shows GIFs and stickers too.

**Find desk phones (administrators).** Administrators can use MonoPhone on a phone, tablet or computer to find desk phones on the local network and provision one to a new or existing extension in one step. Discovered phones also appear in the console (Admin, Devices) with Provision to extension.
**Company phone directory on DECT bases.** Yealink W-series and Gigaset N670/N870 bases now receive the company phone directory (LDAP), so handsets can search colleagues.

**RSA certificate for older phones.** Next to each automatic (Let's Encrypt) certificate the PBX now also obtains an RSA certificate of the same name and gives it to older phones that cannot use the modern certificate, for the web, secure SIP and the phone directory. Admin, Certificates shows both.

**Media encryption is optional on every desk phone.** Provisioned phones of all vendors offer encrypted media (SRTP) but still accept calls without it, on every transport; only the restricted-network profile requires it.

**Phone directory on every model.** Every desk phone model with a directory setting receives the company phone directory when it is on, and DECT bases such as the Yealink W52P get the right server names on every account.

**Phone directory diagnostics.** Failed secure directory (LDAPS) connections and sign-ins now appear in the phone's provisioning log and in the TLS failures view, with a hint about what the phone could not accept.
**Key rotation** now also re-encrypts the TR-069 and phone directory passwords.
**Live location** tells MonoPhone how long to wait when updates are sent too fast.

**Live captions in MonoPhone** have a new card: the newest words on top and always visible above the call controls, phrases grouped by speaker, adjustable text size, and Copy, Summarise and Key points in one menu.
**MonoPhone call readiness** follows the line, so "Calls can't reach this phone" no longer stays on screen after the line is ready.

**Yealink desk phones and DECT handsets (for example the W60B) ended calls with "Error (Media)".** The provisioning file now writes codec settings in the form current Yealink firmware expects. Htek, Fanvil and Cisco codec and encryption settings were corrected too, and Grandstream, Snom, Poly and the other vendors were checked.
**Voicemail (`*86`) could fail because prompts were missing.** The voice prompts now ship with the media service, are checked at start and fall back to English when a language is missing.
**Push-to-talk on iPhone and Mac.** Your voice now reaches the channel, and iPhone receives and plays transmissions. The priority mark is no longer shown as a warning.
**Live location** keeps updating on iPhone when you stand still and keeps sending on Android.
**Live captions** now hide when you turn them off, and on-device captions no longer show "Reconnecting".

releases.summary: Desk phones and DECT bases that place calls with sound, the company phone directory on more phones, voicemail prompts that always play, faster push-to-talk, stickers in team chat and a quicker start for new companies.

items: **Leave push-to-talk from the Keypad.** When you are in a push-to-talk channel, the pill on the MonoPhone Keypad has a Leave button next to the channel name.
**Quieter push-to-talk channel page.** Past voice messages are hidden by default; Show recent messages opens them, and MonoPhone remembers your choice for each channel.
**Revealing phone credentials** in Devices no longer asks you to sign in again. The permission to see device secrets decides who can reveal them; every reveal is still recorded in the audit log.

**Phone address always available.** Administrators allowed to see device secrets find the phone's provisioning address, with a Copy button and its login when one is needed, in the phone's settings on the desk phones page and in Reveal credentials, for every provisioned phone. Others are offered Regenerate to get a new address.
**Desk phones page.** The desk phone time and codec settings and the vendor redirect servers now sit in a collapsed Advanced section, which remembers whether you opened it.
**Yealink phones behind NAT.** Provisioned Yealink desk phones and DECT bases now turn on rport, and DECT handsets also send a NAT keep-alive, so calls keep working behind routers.

**Some desk phones and DECT bases (for example the Yealink W60B) registered but could not place calls.** Calls stayed on "calling" with no sound because the phone did not answer the call sign-in request. These phones now get a sign-in request they understand.
**Click-to-call** no longer sends an extra update to your own phone once the other party is connected.

releases.summary: Calls from DECT bases such as the Yealink W60B, an easier push-to-talk pill in MonoPhone and a tidier desk phones page.

items: **Every Yealink desk family and the W-series DECT kits.** Provisioning recognises all current Yealink desk phones (including expansion modules) and the W-series DECT bases and handsets such as the W60B, with the right time zone and daylight saving time and the base's web login.
**Every current Grandstream family.** GXP, GRP, GXV, WP, the DP75x DECT bases and the HT analogue adapters are provisioned with time zone, language, codecs, line keys and the phone book.
**More phone vendors.** New templates for Gigaset Pro DECT (N510, N670, N870), Cisco IP DECT 110/210, Panasonic, Mitel, Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise, Akuvox and Avaya J100.
**A unique web password for every phone.** Each provisioned phone gets its own web page password instead of a shared default.
**Reveal credentials.** Devices has a Reveal credentials action for the SIP account, the phone web page and the phone directory, protected by a fresh sign-in check.

**Phone directory on desk phones.** A read-only company directory (LDAP over TLS) is provisioned on desk phones and is on by default. Work e-mail addresses stay hidden from phones unless you switch them on.
**Remote phone management (TR-069).** A company switch (off by default) lets MonoPbx manage supporting phones remotely: status, parameters, reboot and resync actions, bulk actions and firmware jobs.
**Re-enrolment after a factory reset.** A phone that was reset to factory settings waits in a re-enrolment queue so an administrator can hand it its configuration again.
**Phone-screen apps.** Desk phones with an XML browser get MonoPbx apps on the phone screen, reachable from a free line key.

**Voicemail key and message lamp everywhere.** The voicemail key and the message waiting lamp work on every supported desk phone and DECT handset, including phones that never subscribe for message alerts.
**Texts between phones.** Desk and DECT phones can text each other, and their texts reach MonoPhone chat and SMS.
**Do not disturb and forwarding stay in sync** between the phone and MonoPbx, and forward dial codes work from desk phones.

**More desk phone features:** the connected caller's name after a transfer, distinctive ring tones, BLF pickup, a record key, keep-alive for phones behind NAT, intercom auto-answer, a second registrar for failover, the company certificate authority, and Opus as an opt-in codec.

**Twilio-compatible call scripts.** Calls created through the Twilio-compatible API can run TwiML, including live updates, status callbacks, Dial actions, Say voices and remote Play media. Compiled flows keep their prompts in the prompt library.
**Custom AI prompts.** Tailor the instructions for AI answers per company, feature and channel, with a preview.
**AI answers on delivery orders.** Customers writing about a delivery order can get an AI reply in the order thread.
**Business locations on calls.** Inbound calls are tagged with the business location of the number that was called.

**911 and 112 calls with a dispatchable location.** Calls to 911, 112 and other public safety numbers carry the caller's registered location to trunks that support it, and administrators are alerted when a location is missing.
**Call quality thresholds** are now a company setting.
**Callback order.** Queue callbacks can call the agent first or the customer first; customer first plays a short announcement while the agent is connected.
**Push-to-talk on the Keypad.** MonoPhone shows a push-to-talk pill on the Keypad for quick access to your channels.
**Smart callback:** a "yes" reply on WhatsApp books the callback at any step of the flow.
**Click-to-call** keeps the audio path of your device when the call is answered.
**Call supervision** (listen, whisper, barge) continues after a server restart.
**CRM and Jira call logs** include a link to the recording in the console.
**The browser extension** refreshes order cards when a shop order changes.
**Clinic integrations** use one set of safety rules that cannot be edited away.
**Fanvil, Snom, Poly, Cisco and Htek** provisioning was checked again, with better model detection and resync.
**Test builds of MonoPhone** receive calls through their own push channel.
**Voice fraud protection** now also e-mails the account owner when voice is stopped.
**Provisioning behind the HTTPS front** no longer refuses phones as plain HTTP.
**Apple Watch push-to-talk** wakes correctly for listening, and the call label no longer clips.
**Links on the error code pages** open the right pages.
Security improvements (medium): each phone has its own web password, phone credentials are shown only after a fresh sign-in check, and queue callbacks have per-number and per-hour limits with alerts.

releases.summary: Much wider desk and DECT phone support with a phone directory, remote management and many new phone features, Twilio-compatible call scripts, custom AI prompts, business locations and a dispatchable location for 911 and 112 calls. **Upgrade note:** the phone directory is now on by default. If your desk phones use it, allow 636/tcp (LDAPS) from the phones' networks to the server.

items: **MonoPbx Voice packs, no pay as you go.** Choose the regional minute packs you need as a checklist, in any combination; each pack can be held once. The console (Numbers, MonoPbx Voice, Plan and usage), the account page and the pricing calculator show the ticked packs and their total. Calls to destinations that no pack covers, or after a pack's minutes are used up, are refused with a short announcement instead of being charged. Removing a pack stops it at the end of the current period, with no refund.

**Push-to-talk widgets.** Add a push-to-talk widget to the iPhone Home Screen for one channel or several, with a Talk button per channel, the member count and who is talking. Apple Watch has push-to-talk complications and a Smart Stack widget that open the channel directly.

**Messages on Apple Watch.** Read your chats with unread badges, see photos and the first page of PDF files, play and record voice notes, reply with dictation, Scribble, emoji or quick replies, react and start a new chat. Chat notifications on the watch offer Reply, thumbs-up and Mark read.
**Calls on Apple Watch.** Search people by name or extension and call them, call back from the watch, and see whether a call goes through the watch or the iPhone.

**Push-to-talk on Apple Watch over mobile data.** A watch with mobile data or Wi-Fi can use push-to-talk without the iPhone nearby. It is woken for new talk and shows its connection (Wi-Fi, mobile data or via iPhone) and reconnects on its own.

**Monthly transcription quota.** Set a monthly limit of transcription minutes for the company in Admin, AI, Transcription. Recordings, voicemail, voice notes and live captions count towards it. Administrators are warned at 80 % and mailed at 100 %; new transcriptions then wait until the next month or a higher limit, and nothing is deleted. Admin, AI budgets shows the use per source.
**Speaker labels for mono recordings.** An optional company setting labels the speakers in transcripts of mono recordings.

**Update check settings for every install.** Admin, Updates, Update check settings now works on every kind of install: switch the update check on or off and choose the channel, stored per install. Settings fixed in the server environment are shown as locked.

**Selecting messages in MonoPhone** works like in common messengers: a long press selects a message, taps add more messages, files, photos and voice notes, and the bar offers Forward, Copy, Delete and Share. With one message selected you also get Reply, Pin, reactions and Info. In the console, Forward starts the same selection.

**Sharing to MonoPhone on iPhone** suggests your recent chats in the share sheet, and you can send a share to up to ten chats or people at once. Files are uploaded once; a chat that could not receive the share is named with a retry. Android has the same multi-chat share screen.
**Voicemail transcripts** count towards the new transcription quota, so transcription costs stay predictable.
**Call readiness** in MonoPhone now simply says whether push notifications are Working or Not working, with tips under "Calls not ringing?".
**MonoPhone on macOS** uses the system glass look on macOS 26.
**Fraud protection for MonoPbx Voice** stops voice for the company at once when unusual calling is detected and alerts your provider, who can resume it.

**Push-to-talk** no longer stays on "Connecting…" after joining a channel. A channel that cannot be reached shows the reason and a Try again button, Leave works at any time, and a channel you left shows Join.
**Apple Watch** no longer breaks the line of a held call row on the larger watch sizes.
Security fixes (medium): AI catalogue updates are accepted only when they are signed with a trusted key, and unsigned catalogues are refused.

releases.summary: Simpler MonoPbx Voice packs, reliable push-to-talk with new widgets, messages and calls on Apple Watch, a monthly transcription quota and update settings for every install.

items: **Voicemail on by default.** New extensions get a personal mailbox automatically, whether they are added in the console, by CSV import, by user provisioning, by single sign-on or by configuration as code. Administrators can still switch this off in Admin, Voicemail defaults. Companies that never changed this setting have it turned on with the update. Existing extensions keep what they have.

**Turn on voicemail in the console.** The extension page and the user page have a Voicemail card: turn voicemail on, switch it off again, set e-mail delivery, retention and the message limit, reset the PIN and manage greetings.

**Turn on voicemail for many extensions at once.** Select users or extensions and choose Turn on voicemail, or use Admin, Voicemail defaults, "Create mailboxes for existing extensions without one". The console shows the count first, then the progress, and reports what was created.

**Bring a number.** Request to move your existing numbers to MonoPbx Voice from the account page: enter the numbers and the current provider's details, upload the signed authorisation and an optional bill, and follow the request's status. Available when MonoPbx Voice is enabled by your provider.

**Cancel a number port request.** Cancel a port request from the account page or from the console (Numbers, MonoPbx Voice, Port requests) while it can still be withdrawn. Requests already sent to the carrier show "Cancellation requested" until the carrier confirms.

**MonoPbx Cloud server sizing.** Cloud servers show their size and recent use of memory, disk and load, with advice when the server is getting full and a one-click request for a larger server where the provider supports it.
**Turning MonoPbx Voice off** now also stops your minute bundles from renewing at the end of the current period. There is no refund for the running period.
**MonoPbx Cloud backups** start at staggered times so that cloud servers do not all back up in the same minute, and a server that has not received its backup plan gets it again automatically.
**Audit log** shows the names of people, extensions, devices and API keys instead of identifiers, with shorter times and all filters in the filter bar.
**User search** in the console finds users by name in either order, e-mail address or extension number.
**Live calls** shows a clear message when no calls are in progress.
**Status** buttons are at the top of your settings page, and the inbox uses the same filter bar as other pages.
**Voicemail settings in MonoPhone** are always reachable from Calls, Voicemail. If you have no mailbox yet, the app explains this and lets you, or asks your administrator to, turn voicemail on.
**MonoPhone** offers a ringtone choice on iOS and Android and shows the caller's name and company on incoming calls.

**Call readiness** in MonoPhone no longer keeps showing an old push service error after the service has recovered, and the wake-up rate now counts calls that reached the phone over its live connection.
**Licence check-ins** keep working after the licence service is restored from a backup. Servers are no longer mistaken for copies of another server in that case.

releases.summary: Voicemail on by default, bringing your own numbers from the account page, clearer console pages, and more reliable call readiness and licence check-ins.

items: **Chat: select and forward.** Select several messages and forward them to other chats or straight to a colleague, in MonoPhone and the console. Order and attachments are kept and each message shows "Forwarded". Live locations cannot be forwarded, because they belong to the person sharing them.

**Push-to-talk channel "Everyone".** Every company gets a default push-to-talk channel with everyone who has an extension, joined automatically on their devices. People who join or leave the company join or leave the channel.
**Push-to-talk channels in the console.** Create and manage channels and their members in Admin, Messaging, Push-to-talk.
**Add the MonoPhone app from the extension page.** Send a sign-in link or show a QR code for the extension. No MAC address, no new device and no new SIP password are needed.
**Voicemail settings in MonoPhone.** Calls, Voicemail now opens your greetings, voicemail PIN, e-mail delivery and transcription settings directly.
**Favourites in your order.** Drag favourites into the order you want in People, Favourites. The order is shared with MonoPhone and your other devices.
**Alert e-mails.** Toll-fraud, spending and MonoPbx Voice alerts can be e-mailed to administrators who opt in, in their own language, with a limit on how often they are sent.
**Subscriptions and billing.** See your running subscriptions, renewals and payments in the console and the account portal. Prices shown include tax.

**MonoPbx Voice.** Available when enabled by your provider. New permissions for the voice plan and for numbers, a switch to turn the service on or off, one payment card shared with your licence, and requests to bring your own numbers (number porting).
**MonoPbx Cloud backups.** Cloud servers back up to cloud storage without any storage key on the server. An administrator can show the backup key to keep it safe.
**MMS files.** Incoming MMS pictures can be received with a per-provider application key, and files sent over SMPP arrive as text with a download link that expires.
**Liquid Glass on iOS 26.** MonoPhone uses the system's glass look for its tab bar and toolbars on iOS 26.
**Google AI example.** The AI setup guide now shows how to use Gemini and Google Cloud Speech.
**Live captions** remember your language, start faster and recover more reliably after network changes.
**Chat videos** start playing at once while they load, and round video notes can be turned into text.
**Live location sharing** updates every 10 to 30 seconds, can be stopped from the Android notification, and stops when you sign out. The console shows a read-only card.
**Sign-in links** show "Signing you in..." while the app or console finishes signing in.
**MonoPhone design.** Me, the four tabs, call screens, people, messages and sign-in follow the new design more closely. Hints under settings are never cut off in long languages.
**Colours.** Busy and Do not disturb are shown in amber, not red. Green and red are used only for calls and hanging up, in the app and the console.
**SIP domains.** Each SIP account belongs to one domain, which is also its sign-in realm, so phones on your own SIP domain register cleanly.
**AI assistant tools** can read more of your settings, and company-wide limits and confirmation steps protect changes.
**Licence check after a restart.** A server that restarts no longer risks being reported as running on another server.
**Language of system messages.** Security notices and announcements in Messages show in each reader's language.
**Admin menu on foldable iPhones.** The Admin and Supervisor menu now lays out correctly on both screens and in every hinge position.
Security fixes (high): sign-in protection for connected AI assistants was strengthened, and changes made through them now require the latest version of a setting. Update soon.

releases.summary: Forwarding in chat, a default push-to-talk channel, easier MonoPhone sign-in for users, voicemail settings in the app, better live captions, and subscriptions you can see and manage in one place.

items: **MonoPhone works offline.** Recent chats, contacts and call history are kept in an encrypted cache on the phone, so you can read them without a connection. Messages you write while offline wait in an outbox and are sent when the connection returns. A slim strip at the top shows when you are offline.
**Chat: voice note transcripts.** Voice notes in chats, text messages and channels can be turned into text, on demand or automatically when your administrator enables it.
**Chat: who reacted.** Each person has one reaction per message, and you can see who reacted with which emoji.

**Chat: pins, edits and search.** Pin up to three messages in a conversation, edit your own message for 15 minutes (earlier versions are kept in the history), and search inside a chat or across all chats, with highlighted matches. Long messages are supported.
**Chat: drafts.** An unsent message is kept per chat, and the Messages list shows "Draft:" next to it.

**Chat: video messages and round video notes.** Send video clips (MP4 or MOV) with a preview picture, or tap the microphone button to switch to the camera and record a round video note that plays in place.
**Chat: live location.** Share your live location for 15 minutes, 1 hour or 8 hours. The card shows a moving pin and the time left, and you can stop sharing at any time.
**Chat: street maps and documents.** Shared places open on a street map, and documents show inside the conversation with a "Save to Google Drive" option.

**Share into MonoPhone from other apps.** Use Share in another app and pick MonoPhone to send text, photos, videos, audio and documents to a chat or a colleague, with a progress indicator and a retry for each file.

**GIFs and stickers.** Teams can send GIFs and stickers from the company's own GIPHY key. This is off by default: an administrator turns it on and enters the key in Admin, Settings, Company, GIFs and stickers, and can choose the content rating.
**WhatsApp-like conversations.** Chats, texts and the inbox share one familiar conversation layout in the app and, at phone width, in the web console.

**MonoPbx Voice: Plan & usage and Numbers.** Available when enabled by your provider. See your minutes bundle and usage, buy minutes and phone numbers, and choose monthly or annual billing, in the console and in the account portal (Voice and numbers). Bundles have a monthly minutes allowance. After it is used, pay-as-you-go rates apply or calls are refused, depending on your setting.
**New pricing calculator.** Choose Cloud or Self-hosted, then users or simultaneous calls, a minutes bundle, phone numbers, and monthly or annual billing, and see the price before you buy.
**MonoPbx Cloud: annual billing.** Pay for a year at once at a lower price than twelve monthly payments, chosen when you create the cloud server.
**Open console from your account.** A button in the account portal signs you in to the console of your server.
**Admin and Supervisor in MonoPhone.** Every Admin and Supervisor screen now follows one page layout, so lists, filters and actions are in the same place everywhere.
**Wear OS call controls.** Hold, transfer, call waiting, swap and keypad on the watch, and numbers shown in phone format.
**Calmer app feedback.** MonoPhone shows one short message above the tab bar and one status strip instead of many hints. The keypad no longer shows line buttons.
**People.** Favourites tab and a details page for each person in the app and the console.
**My status in the console** looks like the one in the app, and the trial notice takes less room.
**Calls from the console** start on the browser phone, or ask which device to call from, instead of ringing all your devices. Home and Admin are easier to use at phone width.
**Web phone** keypad and call screen follow the MonoPhone design.
**Version and build** are shown in What's new and in the app's About page.
**Licence checkout** shows one clear payment result and returns to the same tab.
**Cloud servers** can run on Google Cloud, with backups, monitoring and a staged update channel.
**Cancellations.** Cancellations take effect at the end of the paid period; unused minutes don't carry over.
**Translations.** Several texts in the console and the app were corrected in all supported languages.
**MonoPhone connection on restricted networks.** Secure connections that do not announce a protocol now reach the website normally, and sharing the secure port with other services is optional.

releases.summary: Much richer team chat in MonoPhone, MonoPhone that keeps working offline, redesigned Admin and Supervisor screens, and MonoPbx Voice and Cloud plans you can manage and pay for in the console and the account portal.

items: **Complete updates from the console.** Updating from the console now also installs the release's server tools and configuration files, not only the new images. Your settings and your own files are kept, the download is checked before anything changes, and a failed step puts the previous version back. Fixes that live in the server configuration now reach every server through a normal update.

**Disk space after updating.** The first update from the console now also applies the 7-day limit for the analytics database's internal diagnostic logs on servers installed earlier, and clears old ones before checking free space.
**Calls between desk phones and the web phone** are covered by stronger automatic checks of the audio in both directions.

releases.summary: Updates from the console now bring the whole release, not only the new software images.

items: **A redesigned MonoPhone app.** The app now has four tabs: **Calls**, **Messages**, **People** and **Keypad**. Calls and voicemail share one list (All, Missed, Voicemail), People holds your team, the company phonebook and your own contacts with favourites and a VIP switch, and your photo at the top opens **Me**, where every personal setting is grouped by what you want to do. Phone numbers are written the way people in your country write them.
**A new call screen.** A waiting or held call stays visible at the top, the controls sit in a tidy grid, a small icon shows the connection quality, and tablets show the caller's card beside the call.

**Call assistant roll-out.** Turn the assistant on for a department or the whole company (Admin, Call assistant), optionally so people cannot switch it off. Each person gets a notification when their assistant is turned on. The console also has a shared assistants page, editable rules under My assistant and a "Screen with AI first" option on ring groups.

**Call assistant on your phone.** A call assistant widget shows whether the assistant is on, paused or out of budget (iPhone Home Screen and Lock Screen, Android home screen). On iPhone the live screening banner is driven by the server, and a Focus filter can switch the assistant mode while a Focus is on.
**AI budgets page.** Set spending limits for AI use in one place (Admin, AI, AI budgets).

**More automation steps.** WhatsApp messages can be free text inside the 24-hour window, with a template as fallback. Kommo, Bitrix24 and Odoo can create contacts, leads and tasks and update deals. Automations can use the AI assistants' Google and Microsoft 365 calendars. Click-to-call can ring a group or queue first.
**More caller languages.** The assistant follows callers in 28 more common languages.
**Instagram and Apple Messages for Business.** Both are now described in the guides, and Apple Messages connects through your messaging provider.

**A new web console.** One sidebar replaces the top bar, the long More menu and the separate admin menu. **Home**, **Calls**, **Messages** and **People** are the same four places as in the app, and **Me** (your name at the bottom of the sidebar) holds your personal settings. Press **Ctrl K** (Cmd K on a Mac) to find any page, person, queue or ring group and jump to it. On phones the sidebar becomes a tab bar with a Keypad tab.

**Home shows what needs you.** Missed calls grouped by caller with Call back, new voicemail with a transcript line, unread team chats and customer conversations, plus today's numbers, favourites and your queues.

**Calls, Messages and People are one list each.** Call history, voicemail and recordings share one Calls list with a detail panel; team chat, customer conversations, SMS and fax share Messages; the directory, your team, contacts and customers share People. Old addresses open the new pages.

**A redesigned web phone.** The phone is docked at the right edge of the page (it collapses to a thin strip, and becomes a sheet or full screen on small windows). One search finds colleagues, contacts, the company phonebook, queues and groups. An incoming call shows a card on any page, and the call screen has a waiting-call card, a held-call row, a call-quality icon and a tidy control grid, like the app.

**The admin console in eight sections.** Overview, People and devices, Numbers and trunks, Call handling, Contact centre, Messaging, AI, Monitoring and reports, and Settings, with at most seven entries each. Related pages are tabs of one page. Every old address still works. Call flows (menus, call flows, automations and personal flows) are one list with a Type filter.

**An admin status board.** The Overview shows live tiles (calls now, agents, queue waits, phones online, trunks, licence seats), **Needs attention** with a Fix button that opens the exact page, **Live now**, calls per hour against the same weekday last week, and recent changes with who made them.

**Standard lists and a Save bar.** Lists across the admin console share one look: live search, filter chips kept in the address, sortable columns, a "..." menu on each row, bulk actions, Show more, and cards on phones. Settings pages share a sticky **Save bar** that shows unsaved changes.

**Restricted networks.** Desk phones on networks that block or break SIP can register with **SIP over TLS on port 443**, shared with the web console, or through the **built-in VPN** with a certificate per phone. Switch either on or off in the console (Admin, Restricted networks), run the built-in checks, and choose the network path per device; provisioning profiles are included for all supported desk phone brands.

**Widgets and Live Activities.** MonoPhone has widgets for favourites, missed calls, voicemail, your status (one tap for Do not disturb), the call assistant and, for supervisors, the live queue, on iPhone and Android. iPhone adds Lock Screen versions, an administrator widget and Live Activities for a call in progress and for call screening. Widget names and labels follow the language of the phone.

**eSIM in MonoPhone.** My eSIMs (Settings) shows when each eSIM was last seen, lets you switch mobile data on or off for sponsored eSIMs, and a notification opens My eSIMs straight away when an administrator makes an eSIM ready to install.

**MonoPhone extras.** Connect your Google account from the app (Me, Account), import and export the company phonebook as CSV with a preview, and on Android show messages in your language and summarise a recorded call, both on the phone itself.

**Video and screen-share links for customers.** From the phone panel (More, Video link) or a conversation, send a customer a link by SMS, in the conversation or by e-mail. The customer opens it in a browser with no app and no account, agrees to the notice, and talks face to face or shares their screen. The agent can record the session only with the customer's consent. Links expire after 30 minutes by default and a session lasts at most four hours.

**Website widget with an AI button.** On a live chat channel routed to an AI agent, visitors get an AI button, and the host page is told when it opens, a message is sent and a reply arrives (never the text). New per-channel protection: hCaptcha or Turnstile, a visitor address read through your trusted proxies, and a chat transcript mailed only when the visitor asks.

**Extension sign-in for every user.** The click-to-call browser extension now signs in with single sign-on for any user, not only roles that control other people's calls; it can only place calls from your own extension.
**Pictures in text messages.** MMS pictures show in the console and in MonoPhone, and are kept with the conversation.
**Apple Watch transfers and call waiting.** The watch app can transfer a call (blind or attended), handle a second call (answer and hold the first, swap, end), and reports call quality.

**More integrations.** Zendesk and ServiceNow connect with sign-in instead of pasted tokens. Calendly and a second booking tool, ServiceTitan, Jobber, Zendesk, Freshdesk and ServiceNow events reach automations, the call assistant's own bookings raise appointment events, and a field-service job can give the number to call. Kommo and Bitrix24 log calls (with the recording link) and show e-mail, phone and company in the pop-up.

**Company SIEM export and lead list.** A company can send its audit events to its own SIEM, with a health check and a dropped-events alert. Real-estate and clinic leads have their own list under Admin, Integrations.

**More telephony.** A silenced number routed to a ring group goes to the group's no-answer destination without ringing. Queues skip agents in Do not disturb unless the caller is a VIP, and callback numbers are checked against the do-not-call lists before every attempt. Callers refused for the simultaneous-call limit hear a spoken message. A media session that loses its port is moved to a new one in a live call. Hot-desk and conference prompts have audio in all nine languages, and IVR input hand-offs can send headers and map the answer.

**More messaging.** Meta channel tokens are watched and an alert appears seven days before they expire. Template messages can be sent again after the 24-hour window. Chinese, Japanese and Thai conversation search finds whole words. A reached SMS cap also notifies administrators on their phones. Call keypad shortcuts (send a digit while on a call) can be chosen in the web console and in MonoPhone.

**Platform.** Terraform can read a device's SIP credentials without keeping them in state, the PBX answers the relay's proof-of-work request on enrolment, and a Helm chart and cloud image sources are included.

**More for administrators.** Trunk forms control how inbound calls are identified (number, caller and host); queue pause, wrap-up and available times are kept for reports; an assistant's desk phone gets a key for each executive; Cisco phones follow the company language; exported recordings say whether the caller heard the recording notice; storage compliance holds now work on Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob; and a language chosen in a call flow menu reaches live translation.

**The console finished everywhere.** The **Calls** hub has more filters (direction, dates, number or extension, tag), one Export menu and a row menu (add contact, block, create a Jira issue, save or delete a recording). Call history, voicemail and recordings are standard lists with a player in the row. Chat has one search box and a "+" for a new chat, and the inbox shows one icon and one badge per conversation and opens the first conversation on wide screens. Contacts have an empty state with **Add contact** and **Import CSV**.
**Supervisor control.** Listen, Whisper and Barge are one segmented control, and each agent's state is a pill with a Status menu.
**Reports with tabs, tiles and a chart.** Extensions, Queues, Quality and Scheduled are tabs, with tiles for the period, a ranking chart, a totals row and a column picker.
**Settings home with search.** Search finds pages, settings and their usual names, and each category lists its sections with **Open here** (the real form) or **Open full page**.
**Numbers and trunks.** Numbers show **Where it rings**, with an empty state that offers **Add your first number**, and each trunk has a status card (state, latency and channel limit).
**Agent login and logout codes moved to Dial codes** (Settings, Telephony). Queues links to the new place.
**Toasts with Undo, a globe language menu and your photo on Me.** Short confirmations offer **Undo**, the sign-in page has a globe menu to choose the language, and the Me button shows your photo.
**Upgrades help without a shell.** The Upgrades page explains how to update from the server's command line with a copy button and a link to the guide.

**MonoPhone sign-in and forms.** First sign-in leads with **Scan QR code**. Forms have labels above fields and are grouped into sections, the Me page is reorganised by what you want to do, pages show skeleton placeholders while loading, there are new dialogs, the supervisor pages follow the redesign, and one icon set is used everywhere. Call assistant counters show on the assistant pages.

**Redesigned Apple Watch and Wear OS apps.** Both have Calls (recent calls and voicemail, with All, Missed and Voicemail on Apple Watch), People, Keypad and Me. Numbers are formatted like on the phone, Me offers Available, Busy and Do not disturb, and "Ready" shows only when something needs fixing. Apple Watch shows a compact call-waiting card and a slim held-call row, and both watches follow larger text sizes.

**Licence sign-up in the setup wizard is checked end to end.** Signing up, confirming your e-mail, signing in and receiving the trial licence with its end date are now tested automatically on every build, against a real licence service.

**Console lists and forms everywhere.** Settings pages (Security, Recording, Logging, Transcription limits, Storage, Backups, Companies, AI settings, Integrations) share the sticky **Save bar**, and many more pages (Calling profiles, Door phones, Hotel, Hot desking, Park slots, Shared voicemail, Phonebook, Executives, Backups, Legal holds, Languages, Support, Export jobs, Partners, Companies, Device extras and others) use the shared list with search, filters, a "..." row menu, empty and error states, and cards on phones. Forms that sat beside a list now open in a dialog.

**One page header and calmer status colours.** Every page uses the same heading, with its actions beside it. Status chips no longer use call-green or hang-up-red: enabled and failed states use the accent and warning colours.

**Dark mode, phone width and readability.** Colours that stayed light in dark mode now follow the theme, dimmed hint text is easier to read, and filters, toolbars and forms no longer run off a phone screen in German or Russian.
**Setup bar.** The set-up box on Overview is one line: steps done, progress, the next step and Continue setup.

**Calmer colours and keypad in MonoPhone.** Green always means call, red means end or decline, and every switch uses the same accent colour. Lists show placeholders while loading and say clearly which list failed.
**Readiness and forwarding.** Call readiness shows only what needs fixing. Forwarding has a quick set-up (ring my mobile too, voicemail after 20 seconds, forward everything).
**Paging a group no longer rings members twice.** Members that answer join the page once.
**Failed secure SIP connections** are now listed with the reason next to other unattributed failures, and incoming caller-certificate revocation lists are checked.
**Safer concurrent editing in the API.** More settings now require the current version when you change them and refuse an out-of-date edit, and long lists are paged (see the API guide).
**Media sessions survive a restart** of the media service, including call recordings.

**Keyboard shortcuts.** `l`, `m` and `c` now open Calls, Messages and People. Custom bindings of shortcuts that no longer exist are reset to the defaults. Old console addresses (history, voicemail, recordings, chat, inbox, SMS) redirect to the new pages and keep their filters.

**Clearer colours, names and numbers in the console.** Green is only for call and answer, red only for hang up, decline and missed. Phone numbers are written the way people in your country write them, names come before numbers, times are relative, and empty values show a dash instead of a raw placeholder. Loading lists show placeholders.

**API conventions (for API users).** Changing a stored setting requires the current version in `If-Match` (the server answers 428 when it is missing and 412 when it is out of date) and returns a new `ETag`. More lists use cursor paging (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`), including music-on-hold playlists, Jira call-log entries and the new call groups list. If your integration edits settings or reads long lists, check the API guide. A new status board endpoint backs the Overview.
**Notifications** show phone numbers grouped for every country, and a paged group keeps members that were woken by a push as listeners.

**Assistant translation.** Each assistant can turn live translation of its phrases on or off, and translated phrases are cached per company. The call page can summarise a call on the phone from its transcript.
**AI.** The WhatsApp confirmation template is checked when you save, and conversation search finds old segments without a database extension.
**Standard lists and Save bars on every remaining page.** The last raw tables use the shared list, and the remaining settings forms use the sticky **Save bar**.
**A distinct success colour.** Successful and enabled states use their own colour, separate from call-green.

**A stricter, more accurate API description.** The API document now states the length, range and pattern limits the server enforces, and documents more responses (for example a 201 on first save and 429 on chat routes). For API users: optional query parameters are no longer nullable (a null used to be sent as the text "null"), and a storage destination requires a name.

**Disk filling up over time.** The analytics database kept its own internal diagnostic logs forever, which could fill a small server's disk and block upgrades. It now keeps them for 7 days, and an upgrade clears old ones before it checks for free space.
**File dialogs closing.** Choosing a file again, or cancelling the file chooser, no longer closes the whole dialog (a second contacts import lost its dialog).
**Saving the Company step of setup** was refused when the country also changed the time zone; it now saves.
**Menus in lists** closed on their own right after being opened by an automated click or a small scroll; they stay open.
**Waiting calls on the call screen** were drawn under the buttons on small phones; they are now always visible.
**Installing a personal call-assistant template** for someone without an assistant no longer shows a misleading message.
**Several setting pages** showed raw `undefined` or untranslated placeholders; they now show a dash or a clear message.
**Failed secure SIP connections** are now kept for 30 days per company, so the list survives a restart.
**Group paging** no longer drops a member that registers late after a push wake.
**Call flow designer behind the docked phone.** At narrower window widths the canvas, palette and properties panel ran under the phone panel; the designer now adapts to its own width.
**Setup wizard** no longer refuses the Company step on a fresh install, and the Extension step is covered by tests.
**Searches containing a null character** returned a server error; they now answer with a clear validation error.
**Partner routes** now answer errors in the same format as every other route.
**Fax received label** showed a raw key instead of its name; it is translated in all nine languages.
Security fixes (low): the certificate of an incoming secure trunk call is now also checked for revocation (OCSP).
Security fixes (low): the browser extension's sign-in no longer asks for control over other people's calls.
Security fixes (low): video-link tokens are stored only as a hash, expire quickly and are rate limited, and a web chat widget can require a captcha.

Security fixes (low): the e-mail library is updated to fix several published advisories (STARTTLS handling, message formatting and panics), and other dependencies are updated, including a web networking library.

releases.summary: A redesigned MonoPhone app and web console, SIP that works on restricted networks, more control over the call assistant, new automation steps for CRM, WhatsApp and calendars, and safer editing in the API.

items: **Automations v2.** A new visual designer (Admin, Automations) with a palette of steps, typed forms, an expression editor and a trigger picker. New steps cover logic, approvals and notifications, messaging, integrations, calendar and data tables, and placing calls. Every automation keeps a run history and can be tested from the designer before it goes live.
**AI steps and budgets.** Automations can use AI to read, summarise and write text and to make AI-driven calls. Set spending budgets so AI use stays within a limit you choose.
**Template gallery.** 18 ready-made automations (Admin, Automations, Templates) install in a few clicks and can be exported and shared in the new template format.

**AI call assistant and call screening.** The assistant answers and screens incoming calls and shows the caller's reason live. It is available in the MonoPhone app (a live screening screen, a Live Activity on iPhone, an Android notification and a screened calls history), on Apple Watch, the Mac and Windows apps and the web console. A "My assistant" card on the app home screen sets it up in three taps. Administrators control it with a company policy (Admin, Call assistant).
**Guided setup, steps 5 to 18.** The setup guide now walks through the rest of a new installation, with ready templates, direct links to each page and hints for network and NAT settings.

**Meetings and several click-to-call widgets.** Run meetings with your company's own keys, and create more than one click-to-call widget, each with its own target, number, opening hours, languages and analytics (Admin, Meetings and Widgets).

**Legal hold and active/standby failover.** Place users or data under legal hold so nothing is deleted, across recordings, chats and call history. A standby server can take over automatically if the main one fails.

**Customer timeline and AI agents that do work.** A single timeline shows every call, chat and note for a customer (Customers). AI agents can record outcomes, pause recording while card details are spoken, and prepare quotes.
**Internet-down survival.** If the office internet connection drops, calls between local phones and over backup routes keep working. A new page shows the status and what to prepare.

**Latin America and Mexico first.** Mexican numbers, language and common local providers are now the default starting point, and a migration assistant helps move from another system. New guides cover programmable voice and SMS.
**Contact centre.** Agent scheduling, a preview dialer card, national do-not-call lists and consent tracking, and customer details shown to the agent when a call arrives.
**Google Drive and Gmail in chats.** Share Drive files and email threads in chat conversations.
**Push-to-talk on iPhone.** Push-to-talk now works through Apple's own framework, with iOS controls, more Shortcuts actions and Android quick tiles for push-to-talk and the call assistant.
**Presence and door phones.** Custom statuses are shown correctly to other phones, door phones support digest sign-in, and the share of connections reserved for SIP is configurable.
**MonoPhone for Android no longer crashes when it is opened** on release builds.
**Several wording fixes** in the console menus and in a few translated texts.

releases.summary: Automations get a full designer, AI steps and ready-made templates; the AI call assistant reaches every app; setup, meetings, failover and the Android app are better.

items: **Updating from this morning's version works again.** The previous update was refused on installs that had taken this morning's update ("the database is newer than the target"). Nothing was changed by the refused attempt; this update installs normally.

**One invitation sets up up to 10 phones.** A setup QR code, link or code can now be used up to 10 times while it is valid; each use sets up its own device. Signing out on one phone no longer ends the invitation. Ending it is still possible: an administrator revokes it, the user is removed, or the user answers "That wasn't me". The console shows how many more devices the current invitation can set up, and an invitation used 10 times says so clearly.
**Platform clean-ups** from the follow-up list, including storage export resume and setup preferences used across the console and the app.

releases.summary: A corrective update: installs that took the morning update can update again, and one invitation now sets up several phones.

items: **Export jobs.** Admin, Connections, Export jobs: copy recordings, voicemail, call history, team chat with its files, transcripts with AI summaries, SMS and channel messages, the audit log, faxes and reports to one of your storage destinations, once or on a schedule. Choose the folder and file names from templates, audio as WAV or Ogg Opus, tables as CSV, JSONL or Parquet, optionally compressed. Every file is checked after upload and each run leaves a manifest of what it wrote. Install-wide jobs are under Admin, System, Backups.
**Call the customer of a delivery order.** In the inbox, Call customer on a delivery conversation calls the customer through the PBX, in the console and in MonoPhone.

**Ask your PBX.** Contact center, Ask your PBX: ask about your calls in plain language and get the answer as numbers and a chart, with the question that ran shown. Save questions, pin them to the dashboard and have them mailed on a schedule. Department supervisors see only their own departments. Uses your company's own AI model.

**Proactive health.** Logs, Health: early warnings for trunks that degrade or keep losing registration, disks filling fast, late backups and drops in call quality, each with what to do and one-click fixes where possible. The dashboard shows the three most important items; system administrators get an install-wide report.

**Push-to-talk channels.** Channels for a list of people, a department or a team chat group, with talker, listener and supervisor roles, one speaker at a time, a talk limit, supervisor take-over and optional recordings. Members' phones are woken when someone talks. Talking from MonoPhone comes with the app update that supports it.

**Push-to-talk voice notes in chat.** A finished push-to-talk message can be kept as a voice note in the channel's chat group, marked with the channel and time. Chat recordings show a live waveform while you record, and you can pick a place on the map to share.

**AI call assistant.** When you do not answer within the set time, the assistant can take the call, ask the caller who they are and why they call, and then put them through with a whisper, take a voicemail, transfer to a colleague or block the call. VIPs, colleagues and your own devices skip it; an executive's human assistant is tried first. It is also a step in call flows. It follows the caller into nine languages, the disclosure line is optional, and Admin, AI, Usage shows the estimated cost per day.
**Agent skills.** Calls and routing, Agent skills: named skills with levels per agent and skill requirements per queue, with a coverage report. Agents without a required skill are not rung.

**Quality reviews.** Score calls by hand with the same scorecard as the AI, compare manual and AI scores per agent and week, run calibration sessions, and let agents read and acknowledge their own reviews.

**Post-call surveys.** Calls and routing, Post-call surveys: send a short satisfaction or recommendation survey by text message after a queue call, answered on a simple page without sign-in. Results per survey, queue and agent, and alerts on low scores.
**Wallboard and kiosk widgets.** Kiosk widgets with their own queues and service-level thresholds, and per-user widgets and team queues on the wallboard.

**Reseller partners.** Admin, System, Companies, Partners: partners with their own portal to create and manage their companies within a seat allocation, with branding, a usage report and support access that the company approves, declines or revokes on its Support access page.
**Company templates.** Admin, System, Companies, Templates: create a company, its first administrator and its whole starting setup from a versioned template in one step.

**eSIMs for users.** MonoPhone Settings, My eSIMs and the console's My eSIMs show the eSIMs on your own extensions with the data left, and install one on the phone, by QR code or by activation code. Administrators assign eSIMs to users, send install links, issue them again or revoke them on the new eSIM assignments page.

**Automation triggers and limits.** Automations can start from a live call trigger, from their own web address (webhook) or on a schedule, and can be run now by hand. Each company has limits on runs, and administrators are alerted when one is reached.
**On-device AI in MonoPhone.** On supported iPhones and Android phones: summaries, suggested replies and Show in my language, with no text leaving the phone and no AI cost on the server.

**Liquid Glass look in MonoPhone.** A floating glass tab bar and sheets on the newest iOS and macOS, a classic translucent bar on older iOS, an opaque version with Reduce Transparency, and a Material 3 look on Android.

**Android contacts, files and watch.** Colleagues can appear in Android Contacts (Settings, off by default). Recordings, voicemail and chat files can be saved to Files. Wear OS shows presence and unread chats with quick replies, and an On a call widget is available on Android.
**Company blocklist in MonoPhone.** Settings, Admin, Blocklist: view, add, change and remove the company's blocked numbers and prefixes from the phone.

**Voice one-time codes and translation defaults.** One-time codes can be sent by a voice call that reads the code. AI, AI agents, Live translation sets default caller and agent languages per queue, optionally from the caller's country, and can speak the agent's translated sentences into the call. Transcripts can be read translated into your language.

**Inbox attachments.** The console and MonoPhone say what each channel can send as a file, send other kinds as a link, and hide the file button where a channel takes neither. Videos in the MonoPhone inbox play full screen.
**Jira issues from chat.** An issue created from a chat gets an AI summary when call summaries are switched on.

**Console navigation.** Admin settings pages are gathered in one Settings area grouped by category (Company, Telephony, Users and security, Integrations, AI, Storage and compliance, System), with an All settings overview. A menu entry with sub-items now only folds and unfolds; its page is the first sub-item. Every page keeps its address.

**Notifications in MonoPhone.** Chat and SMS notifications can show the start of the message when your company allows it. Missed calls offer Call back and Message, are grouped, and call notifications show the number and a short Call ended note.

**Call screen.** Transfer and Move to another device are under a More button on the MonoPhone call screen, next to Record, Captions and Park. When a call cannot use them they are greyed out with the reason.

**Sign-in.** In MonoPhone and the console, passkey and single sign-on are under More sign-in options below the main Sign in, shown only when the PBX offers them, and the last method you used is remembered.

**Chat in the console.** Photos or initials everywhere in chat, a compact conversation header with Call and a menu, and Shared shown only when there is something shared. The quiet-hours time zone is a searchable list.

**Chat in MonoPhone.** A lean header with only Call and a menu; tap the photo or name for the person's or group's details. Photos that failed to load are tried again, and groups show their picture in the lists.
**Create Jira issue.** In the inbox, call details and voicemail details, in MonoPhone and the console, the button shows only when Jira is connected and you may create issues.

**Settings in the console.** Settings has five tabs: Profile (where you can now change your photo), Calls and devices, Notifications, Privacy and security, and Language and display. Old addresses still work.
**Test connection.** Test on an installed integration now checks an integration in four steps (settings, reachability, read access and AI tools) and gives a hint to fix each failure.

**AI knowledge and receptionist.** Knowledge-base limits are company settings, shown with the current use. A website can be crawled again on demand with a list of what changed. Call history shows a quality panel, and a compliance miss can raise an alert.
**Hand-over summary.** The web phone and MonoPhone show the AI agent's hand-over note on a ringing and an answered call.
**Admin alerts on phones.** Tapping an admin or role alert in MonoPhone opens the matching alert page. Recents shows contact names, and chat forwards keep their images.

**API changes: new endpoints.** Ask your PBX, health reports, push-to-talk channels, agent skills, quality reviews, post-call surveys, reseller partners and support access, company templates, eSIM assignments and installs, automation quotas, webhooks and run now, AI knowledge limits, translation defaults per queue, receptionist re-crawl and translated transcripts.

**API changes: existing endpoints.** Test connection answers also list the steps. Chat messages carry an optional `ptt` field for push-to-talk voice notes. New chat messages accept `null` for optional fields. All changes are additive; new error codes are listed on the error code pages of the documentation.

Sending a location in MonoPhone chat failed with a message about file types; it is sent again, and each failed send now says what went wrong for a photo, file, voice note or location. Chat sheets stay above the keyboard.

A MonoPhone setup link stopped working without a reason after the device it was for was removed (for example by signing out of the app). The setup page now says why a link stopped working and what to do.

MonoPhone Settings, Executive and assistant showed only Could not load on a PBX without that feature. It now says when the PBX needs an update, shows a friendly message when you are neither, and shows the real error otherwise.
Admin and supervisor recordings downloaded but did not play in MonoPhone; they now play, whatever the audio format.
Admin and role alert notifications did not reach phones and browsers; they arrive again.

releases.summary: Export jobs to your own storage, Ask your PBX, proactive health warnings, push-to-talk channels, an AI call assistant, contact-center skills, quality reviews and surveys, reseller partners, eSIMs in MonoPhone and the console, on-device AI and a refreshed look in MonoPhone, and many fixes.

items: **Live call triggers.** Admin, AI, Live call triggers: when a phrase or topic comes up on a live call, alert supervisors, post in chat, send a webhook event, add a CRM note, open a helpdesk ticket, tag the call or show a hint to the person on the call. Six ready-made triggers in nine languages are enabled with one click, and a tester shows what would fire on typed or spoken text. Never stores what was said; needs live assist with a speech provider.

**Custom status.** Make a status of your own with a text of up to 60 characters, an emoji, a colour (available, away or busy) and an automatic end (30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, today or this week). Colleagues see it in Team, in presence and in chat headers, and it can carry forwarding rules like any other status. In MonoPhone and the console.

**Blocklist for calls and SMS.** Block or silence a number, a prefix or withheld numbers, for calls, SMS or both, optionally until a set time. A blocked caller hears rejected, busy or not in service; a silenced call goes straight to voicemail. Block from Recents or Contacts. Each user's list is their own.

**Executives and assistants.** Admin, Calls and routing, Executives and assistants: an assistant screens the calls of an executive (outside callers only, or every caller), with a private line of numbers that always ring the executive. Assistants can set the executive's Do not disturb and forwarding when allowed.

**Door phones.** Admin, Calls and routing, Door phones: SIP door stations ring people inside, show a still image of the camera and open the door with a key press in the call or a relay, also from the Open button in MonoPhone. An office-hours schedule decides when they ring.

**Chat retention, legal hold and export.** Admin, Chat retention: a company retention period with the shortest and longest period a chat may set, and whether group owners and admins may set their own. Place a legal hold on a chat or a person (nothing is deleted while it lasts) and export a chat as PDF, JSON or ZIP with its attachments. Members see the period in force and any hold in the console and in MonoPhone.

**Number porting.** Admin, Calls and routing, DIDs, Number porting: keep a port request in one place (numbers, account at the old carrier, the signed letter of authorisation, dates and carrier answers) with reminders. On the confirmed date the numbers join the chosen trunk by themselves.

**Caller-ID names.** Admin, Calls and routing, DIDs, Caller names: the name each of your numbers shows on outgoing calls, and names for incoming outside callers looked up in the directory, company contacts and other sources.

**Recording policies and card-payment pause.** Admin, Recording: policies per company, site, extension, user, queue, number or trunk, with never, on demand and a percentage of calls. Pausing for a card payment can also hide the keys pressed while the recording is paused.

**Storage compliance.** Admin, Backups, Storage status: one page for the backup state, extra backup copies on other storage destinations with their own schedule and retention, write-once storage and legal hold, signed manifests that prove a backup is unchanged, and alerts when a backup fails or is late. Also in MonoPhone's admin status.

**AI admin copilot.** AI, Admin copilot in the console, and Settings, Admin, Copilot in MonoPhone: configure and troubleshoot the PBX in plain language. It looks things up with your permissions, shows every change as a preview before you apply it, logs it in the audit log and undoes a whole change set in one step. Uses your company's own AI model.

**PBX updates in MonoPhone.** Settings, Admin, PBX updates: the installed version, Check for updates, the What's new notes of every newer version, and Install update with progress, for administrators with the matching permission.

**Rich chat notifications.** Chat notifications on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android show the sender's name and photo and are grouped per chat. Notifications never carry the message text through the push service.

**Better browser notifications.** Answer or decline a ringing call and reply to a chat message from the browser notification; one counted notification per chat and per SMS conversation; the sender's initials as the icon; admin alerts named by kind that open the right page. On iPhone and iPad, Safari shows how to add the web phone to the Home Screen.
**Hours for one date.** Office-hours schedules can have different hours for a single date. In MonoPhone, changing Today's hours applies to today only by default.
**Password reset by e-mail.** Admin, Users: Send password reset mails a single-use link valid for one day. Also in MonoPhone's admin user page.

**One kind of chat.** A chat is now a direct message or a group. A group has two plain settings: Who can post (everyone or only admins) and Who can join (invited people only, anyone can ask to join, or anyone in the company). New groups take a name, photo and description. One list with All, Unread, Groups and Direct filters, and error messages that say what went wrong where it happened.

**New Messages screen in MonoPhone.** A lean header with only New and a menu, one search field, one row of small filters, Archived chats folded into one row at the top, Mark all as read, and a clear reason when team chat is not available.

**Admin and Supervisor menus in MonoPhone.** Both sections now open a side menu from the menu button or an edge swipe, with grouped entries, badges for counts and Back to MonoPhone at the bottom. Tablets show the Supervisor menu as a side list.

**Contact and call details in MonoPhone.** Actions are shown as tiles that wrap instead of being cut, list rows keep only the Call button and open the details on tap, colleague and contact details list recent calls with that person, and About shows the version with Check for updates on one tile. MonoPhone also works better with older PBX versions.
**Finish setup box.** While setup steps remain, a box at the top of the admin home shows how many are left and continues with the next one. It can be collapsed, or hidden for the whole company.

**Call flow editor.** A palette of components grouped by kind sits next to the canvas. Remove a node with its ×, the Delete key or Delete node (with a confirmation when it has connections, and undo), and a click on a node opens its properties.

**Call pull is clearer.** Dialling `*85` when there is no call to pull now says "No call to pull" instead of reporting an unknown feature code, and MonoPhone shows the pull button only when one of your calls can be pulled.

**Integrations page.** Admin, Integrations shows a searchable list next to the details of the selected integration: what it does, the data it reads and writes, its permissions and settings. The install form puts required fields first and masks stored secrets.

**Single sign-on.** While single sign-on is required, accounts without a system role are given no password, and the sign-in pages say so. Accounts created on first sign-in get an extension from a range you choose, SAML group claims can also set the department, and identity providers with ECDSA keys are supported.
**Sites.** A new phone joins its user's site, or the site whose network it is provisioned from. A site you choose by hand is kept.

**Web phone ringing and closing.** Outgoing calls in the web phone play a ringback tone until answered (or the network's own tones), the ring volume can be set, and an × closes the phone. During a call it asks whether to keep the call in the background or hang up, and never hangs up by itself.

**MonoPhone polish.** Opening the Admin section asks only for your passkey when you have one, with no separate password. Chat and SMS headers show the other person's photo or the group picture, Team shows a colleague's custom status emoji on their photo, and keypad tones moved to Advanced settings.
**BI feed ready out of the box.** Admin, BI feed: the feed is set up by the installer and the updater, so you only create a BI user; no server settings to edit.
**Toll-fraud limits per calling profile.** Calling profiles can set their own limit on simultaneous international calls and calls per hour at night.
**Dialer campaigns.** A compliance page per campaign shows calling-window checks and the abandoned-call rate; contacts can be edited and imported from a file, and opt-outs imported from CSV.

**API changes.** On chat message tasks the field `external_key` is now `external_ref`. Chat lists (mentions, starred messages, threads, the Shared tab, reactions, scheduled messages, reminders) are paged with `cursor` and `next_cursor`; the `before` and `before_seq` parameters were removed. Following threads, starring, chat settings, company chat controls, poll votes, scheduled messages and reminders now require `If-Match` when changed, and their answers carry a `version`. Update scripts and integrations that use these.
SIP trace now captures calls made from MonoPhone and the web phone on installs where the console and the call engine run on separate servers; such traces showed no calls before.
Install update in Admin, Updates showed the previous update as already installed and stopped; it now shows the progress of the new one at once.
MonoPhone: Make default now switches the line, the keypad and outgoing calls to that account at once and is remembered at the next start. It is shown only when the phone has more than one account.
Backups failed on installs updated to the version with sites; they run again.
Profile photos uploaded from MonoPhone showed as broken images in the console.
MonoPhone: call recordings and voicemail in the Admin and Supervisor sections now play on iPhone and Android, from the loudspeaker, and an error says exactly why a file cannot be played.
MonoPhone: a phone set up with a setup code no longer asks for a password sign-in.
Security fixes (low): sign-in and account protection, and data separation between companies.

releases.summary: Live call triggers, custom statuses and a personal blocklist, chat retention with legal hold and export, executives with assistants, door phones, number porting, caller-ID names, an AI admin copilot and a simpler chat and Messages screen in MonoPhone.

items: **SIP trace.** Admin, Logs, SIP trace: trace one extension, trunk or number, or a caller, called number or address, for a set time and with limits on calls, messages and size. Watch the messages live as a ladder diagram, open any message in full, search, and download a pcap file per call or for the whole trace.

**Readable SIP events.** Admin, Logs, SIP events: each line opens into the request and every response. A sign-in challenge and its retry are shown as one line, and a reason code explains in plain words why a call failed. Links start a trace of the extension or the peer, or open the call. SIP events now also name the trunk.

**Toll-fraud protection.** Admin, Call routing, Toll fraud and CLIR (Toll-fraud policy): built-in lists of high-risk destinations and premium numbers, your own blocked and allowed prefixes (or allow listed destinations only), a night-time limit, a limit on simultaneous international calls per user, and an automatic temporary block when international calls suddenly spike. Current blocks are listed there and can be lifted.

**Action after updating: high-risk calls are refused.** Calls to the built-in high-risk destinations and premium numbers are refused until an administrator allows them in Admin, Call routing, Toll fraud and CLIR (Toll-fraud policy). Allow only the destinations your company really calls.

**Chat announcement channels, webhooks and rich cards.** Announcement chats where only chat admins post (members can still react), chat admins and pinned messages, and webhooks per chat so other systems can post messages and rich message cards into a chat. In the console and in MonoPhone.

**Chat: mute and delete.** Mute a chat for 8 hours, a week, until a chosen time or until you turn it back on, and still be notified when someone mentions you if you like. Delete a message for yourself or for everyone (within 48 hours; moderators at any time), or clear a chat for yourself.

**Chat channels, groups and media.** Every company gets What's new, General and Announcements channels; What's new shows the release notes of each installed update. Create groups and channels with a description, picture and visibility; find, join or ask to join them; pin and archive chats. Send photos, videos, your location and voice notes, and share files through links that expire.

**MonoPhone admin section.** Administrators can now manage the PBX from MonoPhone (Settings, Admin): users, phone setup, devices and who is online; live calls, office hours, forwarding, queues and IVR; system status with push alerts for administrators, company call history with the readable SIP view, and the audit log; voicemail and recordings; SMS, eSIM and licence (view only). Each screen appears only with the matching permission, and the server checks every action as it does for the console.

**Passkeys in MonoPhone and confirmation for admin actions.** Sign in to MonoPhone with a passkey on iOS, macOS and Android, with the same passkeys as the console. Before opening the app's Admin section and before destructive admin actions, MonoPhone asks for a passkey, or the password and the second factor; a confirmation stays valid for ten minutes. Switch it in Admin, Security.

**"That wasn't me" notices.** When a QR code, setup link or setup code is used to set up a device, the user and the administrator who issued it get an e-mail and a chat message from MonoPbx Security with the device, the approximate country, the address and the time. "That wasn't me" removes the device and ends its sign-ins at once.

**Live captions.** Supervisors can turn on live captions for a queue call on the supervisor page, recognised on the server with the company's speech provider. Captions reach only the people on the call and the supervisors who joined, and an announcement tells the callers first. Rules in Admin, AI calls: consent, transcripts and verification codes; saving the captions as a transcript is off by default and has a retention period. Switch the feature on in the AI settings.

**Storage destinations.** Send files to Amazon S3, S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob storage, for the whole install (Admin, System, Install storage destinations) or per company (Admin, Storage destinations). Encryption options, write-only credentials, and a Test connection button that names any missing permission. Every upload is checked after it is written, and the local copy is released only then.

**App update checker.** MonoPhone tells you when a newer version is available in the App Store or Google Play, and the PBX can set a minimum and a recommended app version. About now shows the real app version.

**Siri, Shortcuts and Live Activity on iPhone.** Ask Siri or use Shortcuts to call a colleague or a number, set your status or hear who is on a call. During a call, the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island offer Mute and Hang up and show "Reconnecting…" while the call recovers.

**Ongoing-call card on Android.** The call notification shows the timer (also on hold), "Reconnecting…" while the call recovers and a Mute button that works on the lock screen. Calls can be added to the phone's call log, and Bluetooth, car audio and holding for a mobile call go through the system.
**Second-factor banner.** The console shows a red banner while your account has no second factor (an authenticator app or a passkey), with a link to set one up.

**What's new in the console.** Admin, Updates now shows the release notes of every version newer than the one installed, next to the Update button and in the confirmation, and shows what changed right after an update.

**Default speech model per AI provider.** In Admin, AI, Providers you can set the speech-to-text model a provider uses by default and see which kind of credential it holds. A model chosen on a feature still takes precedence.

**Profile photos in MonoPhone.** Change your own photo in MonoPhone (Settings, My profile: take a photo or choose one, then crop it). Colleagues' photos now appear in Contacts, Recents, call screens, voicemail, Messages and Chat.

**Reconnecting during calls.** When a phone's connection drops for a moment, MonoPhone shows "Reconnecting…" in place of the call timer and restores the audio by itself; the timer continues where it was. The PBX also notices when one side of a call stops sending audio and asks the app to reconnect.

**Chat collaboration.** In the console and in MonoPhone: react with any emoji and see who reacted; reply in threads and follow them; mention `@all` or `@here` where the chat allows it, and find your mentions in one list; sent, delivered and read ticks with "Seen by"; forward messages to up to 10 chats; link previews; start a group voice or video call from a chat and join a running one; a Shared tab with the media, files, voice notes and links of a chat; saved messages; and polls.

**Chat: plan, prioritise and get help.** Send a message later and set reminders; mark a message as urgent; summarise, translate and draft replies with AI (always labelled); create a task in a connected system from a message; and set your own quiet hours and out-of-office answer.
**Chat controls.** Admin, Messaging, Channels, Chat controls: set company rules for read receipts, link previews, urgent messages and who may mention everyone.

**Sites.** Admin, People, Sites: group departments, users, devices, trunks and numbers into sites, each with its own country, time zone, address and music on hold.
